evidence: A separate fresh context reviewed the sign-in module, auth routes, all migrations, user-role definitions, dependency boundary, module-resolution configuration and review scripts. No findings remained.
The review reran 41 sign-in and digest tests against disposable Postgres. Supplied evidence showed all 106 focused sign-in, digest, permission and lint-boundary tests, TypeScript and ESLint passing.

Signed stub tokens through the real handler prove member access and rejection of Microsoft guests, missing membership claims and string membership values, including guests using the company identity provider.

Before the fix, the shadow entry point, later migration and TypeScript and Next.js alias regressions all failed. The matching tests now pass, as do inherited-configuration and alternate-configuration regressions.

Invited, uninvited, expired, revoked and staff email-link requests have identical status, headers and body. Only the invited outsider receives mail, and local sequential request durations differ by less than 100 ms.

The production entry-point test proves mail is deferred until after the generic response and SMTP failure logs no address or token. The review checked the installed Next.js response-closure scheduling and Better Auth token path.

The existing permission tests pass for authentication tables, administrator-only invitations and the database role boundary. Earlier integration evidence covered files, queued effects and planted privilege faults; this fix does not change their implementations.
limits: No real directory registration, SMTP delivery or hosted storage permissions were exercised.
The local production build could not resolve the pre-existing dependency symlink outside the project root. GitHub build and full-suite results are recorded in the pull request.
The delivery test mocks Next.js after; its production lifecycle was checked through installed source and documentation. Deferred delivery is not a durable queue.
Timing evidence covers local sequential requests. Response padding does not guarantee constant timing under load.
The review reran 41 tests and read supplied evidence for the other focused checks. The digest verifies content correspondence, not reviewer identity; GitHub review independence remains unverified.
